items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Teddy had changed a few musicians since I left the band in 1935... a young 18-year old trumpet played named John Burks Gillespie whom the other fellows in the band called Dizzy.

ctx.x: Willie's orchestra was working at the Ambassador which was a part of the Ambassador Theatre across the street from the American Embassy at Place de la Concorde. Shortly after I had rejoined Willie, Teddy Hill and his band came to Paris with a Cotton Club Revue and played quite a few weeks at the Moulin Rouge at Place Blanche. The revue was staged by Clarence Robinson who was very well known in Harlem for staging shows in the Cotton Club, Connie's Inn, the Lafayette Theatre, Harlem Opera House and the Apollo…

Teddy had changed a few musicians since I left the band in 1935. Bob Carroll, ex-Redman alumnus, was on tenor, having replaced Chu Berry; Wilbur de Paris had been added on trombone, and a young 18-year old trumpet played named John Burks Gillespie whom the other fellows in the band called Dizzy. Dizzy had replaced Frank Newton who had come in the band after I left.

My recording activities started the 7th of July when I recorded with Dicky Wells' Orchestra which included Bill Dillard, Shad Collins, who had replaced Roy Eldridge, Dicky, Django Reinhardt, Richard Fullbright on bass and Bill Beeson on drums.
